name: Anandamide
aliases: AEA, 5,8,11,14-Eicosatetraenoylethanolamide, Anandamide (20.4, N-6), Anandamide(20:4, N-6), Arachidonic acid N-(hydroxyethyl)amide, arachidonoyl ethanolamide, Arachidonylethanolamide, N-(2-Hydroxyethyl)anachidonamide
summary: Anandamide (ANA), also referred to as N-arachidonoylethanolamine (AEA), is a fatty acid neurotransmitter belonging to the fatty acid derivative group known as N-acylethanolamines (NAE). Anandamide takes its name from the Sanskrit word ananda (आनन्द), meaning "joy, bliss, delight," plus amide.
